# Mandate Delivery v1 interoperability vector

`mandate-delivery-v1.json` is generated by the real TypeScript resolver through
`backend/test/mandate-delivery.spec.ts` with in-memory D1/R2 and a fixed clock.
The private key is a PUBLIC DETERMINISTIC TEST FIXTURE (32 bytes of 0x01), never a
production key. It must never be provisioned into an installation or issuer.

From `backend`, deliberately set `MANDATE_DELIVERY_UPDATE_VECTOR=1` and run
`node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run test/mandate-delivery.spec.ts` to regenerate.
Unset that variable afterwards. Ordinary tests only read and reproduce the vector;
a stale vector fails byte-for-byte comparison, rather than being updated silently.

Bodies are base64 of exact HTTP JSON bytes. The artifact contains non-UTF-8 bytes.
The negative body is signed under BLOOM-AUTHORITY-SNAPSHOT-v1. `canonical_base64`
contains JCS of the unsigned envelope; `digest` hashes the raw artifact.

Batcave's mandate-delivery-proxy.test.ts transports these exact bodies. Go's
integration_test.go reads this committed vector directly, without Node or network.
Go's other unit tests may sign mutations with the public test fixture key; the
interoperability acceptance test never manufactures its own valid body.

This is injected-dependency receipt verification, not productive bootstrap.
